'''Liberty State Park''' ('''LSP''') is a {{convert|1212|acre|ha}} [[state park]] in the [[U.S. state]] of [[New Jersey]], located on [[Upper New York Bay]] in [[Jersey City, New Jersey|Jersey City]] opposite [[Liberty Island]] and [[Ellis Island]]. The park opened in 1976 to coincide with [[United States Bicentennial|bicentennial]] celebrations<ref>{{cite web |url=http://events.norwalkcitizen-news.com/-city-nj/venues/show/10630-liberty-state-park |title=Liberty State Park – Jersey City, NJ – Norwalk Citizen-News |access-date=April 9, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120709080951/http://events.norwalkcitizen-news.com/-city-nj/venues/show/10630-liberty-state-park |archive-date=July 9, 2012 }}</ref> and is operated and maintained by the [[New Jersey Division of Parks and Forestry]]. [[Statue City Cruises]] provides ferry service from the [[Central Railroad of New Jersey Terminal]] to Liberty Island and Ellis Island.

The park is the largest in Jersey City, the largest urban park in the state, the most visited New Jersey state park and one of the most visited state parks in the United States with approximately 4.5 million visitors each year as of 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/news/environment/2024/06/03/things-to-do-outside-in-new-jersey-state-parks/73893966007/|title=It's time to head outside, New Jersey! These are the most visited state parks|website=northjersey.com|date=June 6, 2024|access-date=July 29, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://njcu.libguides.com/libertypark|title=Liberty State Park|website=njcu.libguides.com|access-date=July 29, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://thedigestonline.com/new-jersey/popular-new-jersey-state-park-summer-2025/|title=This NJ State Park Is One of the Most Popular in the U.S.|work=New Jersey Digest|date=August 11, 2025|access-date=August 13, 2025}}</ref>

The main part of the park is bordered by water on three sides: on the north by the [[Morris Canal]] Big Basin and on the south and east by [[Upper New York Bay]]. The [[New Jersey Turnpike#Extensions|New Jersey Turnpike Newark Bay Extension]], which is part of [[Interstate 78 in New Jersey|I-78]], marks its western perimeter.

==Geography==
[[Image:LSP JerseyCity.JPG|thumb|upright=1|The high rise buildings of the [[Jersey City, New Jersey|Jersey City]] skyline as seen from Liberty State Park|alt=]]
Communipaw Cove is part of the {{convert|36|acre|adj=on}} state [[nature preserve]] in the park and is one of the few remaining [[tidal marsh|tidal salt marshes]] along the [[New York Harbor|Hudson River estuary]].
The Nature Center, designed by architect [[Michael Graves]], is part of the preserve. To the west lies the Interior Natural Area, which is off limits to the public and is being allowed through natural processes to recover from environmental abuse.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jerseycityindependent.com/2010/11/12/nature-untamed-liberty-state-parks-interior-natural-area-continues-its-comeback/|title=Nature Untamed: Liberty State Park's Interior Natural Area Continues its Comeback|date=November 12, 2010|website=JerseyCityIndependent.com|access-date=December 8, 2017|archive-date=May 24, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130524184813/http://www.jerseycityindependent.com/2010/11/12/nature-untamed-liberty-state-parks-interior-natural-area-continues-its-comeback/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At the center of the park, 240 acres have been fenced off and contaminated with hazardous materials, such as chromium, arsenic, and petroleum. The six acre train shed is also fenced off and contaminated with asbestos.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/26/nyregion/liberty-state-park-development.html|title=He's Still Fighting Developers for the Park His Father Founded|first=Tracey|last=Tully|newspaper=The New York Times|date=August 26, 2021|access-date=September 13, 2021}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:LibertyStatePark(pre1976).tif|thumb|upright=1|Before opening in June 1976, Liberty State Park was the site of abandoned rail facilities built on landfills.]]
Much of the park is situated on landfilled [[tidal flats]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hudson-Raritan Estuary Comprehensive Restoration Plan – Potential Restoration Opportunities Project Summary Sheets|url=https://www.nan.usace.army.mil/Portals/37/docs/harbor/CRP%20Planning%20Regions/PR_Upper%20Bay__8_2014.pdf|access-date=September 30, 2020}}</ref> In the latter half of 19th century, a small island named [[Black Tom explosion#Black Tom Island|Black Tom]] was joined via landfill with the mainland.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.state.nj.us/dep/parksandforests/parks/liberty_state_park/liberty_blacktomexplosion.html|title=Liberty State Park: Black Tom Explosion|publisher=State of New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection|date=January 26, 2005|access-date=April 8, 2014}}</ref> It became a major shipping, manufacturing, and transportation hub within [[Port of New York and New Jersey]], leading to the construction of [[Communipaw Terminal]]. It was from this ferry/train station that an estimated 10.5 million [[Immigration to the United States|immigrants]], roughly two-thirds that were processed at [[Ellis Island]], entered Jersey City to spread out across the United States.<ref>[http://www.state.nj.us/dep/parksandforests/parks/liberty_state_park/liberty_crrnj.html Liberty State Park: CRRNJ], [[New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection]]. Accessed June 17, 2025.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://njcu.libguides.com/centralrailroad|title=Central Railroad of New Jersey Terminal|website=njcu.libguides.com|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref> In 1916, on what is now the southeastern corner of the park, the [[Black Tom explosion]] killed as many as seven people, caused $20 million in property damage, and was felt throughout the [[Tri-State Region]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://njcu.libguides.com/blacktom|title=Black Tom Explosion|website=njcu.libguides.com|access-date=February 11, 2025}}</ref>

The park was conceived in the 1960s.<ref>{{cite news |last = Mohr |first = Charles |title = Ellis Isle Made National Shrine |newspaper = The New York Times |date = May 12, 1965 |url = https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1965/05/12/101546171.pdf?pdf_redirect=true&ip=0|accessdate = November 5, 2022}}</ref> with the land  transferred from the city to the state in 1965.<ref>{{cite news |date=August 18, 1965 |url=https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1965/08/18/101562148.pdf?pdf_redirect=true&ip=0 |title=Jersey City Deeds Site For Liberty State Park |work=The New York Times |page=32}}</ref> [[Jersey City]] residents Audrey Zapp, Theodore Conrad, Morris Pesin<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hmdb.org/Marker.asp?Marker=13294|title=Morris Pesin's Legendary Canoe Trip Which Launched Liberty State Park Historical Marker|website=HMDb.org|access-date=December 8, 2017|archive-date=December 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171209152439/https://www.hmdb.org/Marker.asp?Marker=13294|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/06/22/nyregion/nyregionspecial2/22colnj.html?scp=39&sq=liberty+island&st=nyt | work=The New York Times | first=Kevin | last=Coyne | title=A Quest That Brought Lady Liberty Closer | date=June 22, 2008}}</ref> and [[J. Owen Grundy]] were influential environmentalists and historians who spearheaded the movement that led to the creation of Liberty State Park.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.folsp.org/grundy_editorial.htm|title=Jersey Journal FOLSP: Jersey Journal|website=FOLSP.org|access-date=December 8, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720184650/http://www.folsp.org/grundy_editorial.htm|archive-date=July 20, 2011}}</ref> They are remembered by the naming of places and streets along the waterfront.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/1976/06/21/bicentennial-beat|title=Bicentennial Beat|first=Mark|last=Singer|date=June 14, 1976|access-date=December 8, 2017|via=www.NewYorker.com}}</ref>

It is estimated the park suffered $20 million in damages during [[Superstorm Sandy]] in October 2012. In June 2016, the Central Railroad of New Jersey Terminal reopened after a $20 million renovation to repair the extensive damage caused by Sandy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2016/06/revamped_liberty_state_park_train_terminal_opens_p.html|title=Historic Liberty State Park train terminal reopens (Photos)|newspaper=The Jersey Journal|last=Villanova|first=Patrick|date=June 22, 2016|access-date=January 11, 2018}}</ref> The Nature Center reopened in June 2021.<ref>{{cite web| last=Ragoza|first=Rafal|title=Latest estimates on Liberty State Park recovery from Hurricane Sandy|newspaper=The Jersey Journal|date=May 25, 2013|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2013/05/latest_estimates_on_liberty_st.html|access-date=May 28, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2015/10/2_senate_democrats_to_hold_hearing_on_future_devel.html|title=Senators want 'secret' DEP report, plan hearing on Liberty State Park's future|last=Villanova|first=Patrick|date=October 2, 2015|website=NJ.com|access-date=December 8, 2017}}</ref>

On January 11, 2018, it was announced by [[New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection]] (NJDEP) that the interior {{convert|240|acre|ha|1}} of the park that have been closed off to the public for decades due to hazardous material and severely [[contaminated land]] would be remediated for the entire community to safely enjoy. The restoration is to be done in phases with the initial phase focusing on a {{convert|23|acre|ha|1}} parcel of the interior.  There is currently no firm timeline yet for the remediation but the funding is to come from natural resource damage settlements.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2018/01/nj_announces_massive_plan_to_restore_240_acres_of.html#incart_river_home|title=N.J. to turn 240 acres of Liberty State Park into wildlife oasis|publisher=The Jersey Journal|last=McDonald|first=Terrence T.|date=January 11, 2018|access-date=January 11, 2018}}</ref> Work was slated to begin in 2021 and ultimately began in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2020/09/shovels-in-ground-next-summer-for-234-acre-cleanup-in-liberty-state-park.html|title=Shovels in ground next summer for 234-acre cleanup in Liberty State Park?|publisher=The Jersey Journal|last=Schmidt|first=Margaret|date=September 3, 2020|website=nj}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2023/10/state-dep-begins-long-awaited-clean-up-and-restoration-of-liberty-state-park-interior.html|title=State DEP begins long-awaited cleanup and restoration of Liberty State Park interior|publisher=The Jersey Journal|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref> In 2024, the NJDEP announced an additional $7.3 million the continued revitalization efforts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hudsoncountyview.com/njdep-reveals-additional-7-3m-for-liberty-state-park-revitalization-at-open-house/|title=NJDEP reveals additional $7.3M for Liberty State Park revitalization at open house|website=hudsoncountyview.com|date=September 28, 2024|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref> In January 2026, the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection announced the start of construction on several projects included in the Liberty State Park Master Plan, including improvements to the Central Railroad of New Jersey Terminal Plaza, development of athletic fields and a picnic area at Marina Green, and restoration of the historic train shed.<ref>https://dep.nj.gov/newsrel/26_0003/</ref>

==Points of interest==
[[Image:Ellis island air photo.jpg|thumb|upright=1|[[Ellis Island]] and the railyards and piers of [[Central Railroad of New Jersey]] before development of the park and associated restoration projects|alt=]]

===Central Railroad of New Jersey Terminal===
On the northern most shore of the park is The [[Central Railroad of New Jersey Terminal|Central Railroad of New Jersey (CRRNJ) Terminal]]. The terminal operated from 1889 to 1964 and also served the Central Railroad of New Jersey-operated [[Reading Company|Reading Railroad]], the [[Baltimore and Ohio Railroad]], and the [[Lehigh Valley Railroad]]. An estimated 10.5 million immigrants that were processed at Ellis Island entered the United States through the station. Today, it serves as a museum and ticket office for [[Statue Cruises|ferry service]] to [[Statue of Liberty National Monument, Ellis Island and Liberty Island|Ellis Island and Liberty Island]] which operates from the Hudson River side of the terminal.

===Freedom Way and Liberty Walkway===
Liberty Walkway, a crescent-shaped promenade, stretches from the CRRNJ Terminal along the waterfront south to the Statue of Liberty overlook, bridging two coves along the way. It is part of the longer [[Hudson River Waterfront Walkway]]. Halfway along Liberty Walkway is a bridge to [[Ellis Island]], but only authorized vehicles are allowed.
The southeastern corner of the park contains the Statue of Liberty overlook, picnic facilities, a playground, the ''U.S. Flag Plaza'' and ''Liberation Monument'', the Public Administration Building, and a memorial to the [[Black Tom explosion]]s. Picnicking and barbecuing facilities are also located at the southern end of the park. Originally called "Liberty Walk",<ref>''Landscape Architecture'' 1991 – Volume 81 Page 69  "The first phase of the park is the {{convert|1.5|mile|km}} waterfront promenade, Liberty Walk. Construction on the promenade has already begun and will be completed in early 1991; "</ref><ref>'' Backroads of New Jersey'' 2007 Page 48 "Take Freedom Way south or walk the {{convert|2|mile|km}} Liberty Walk Promenade through a thirty-six-acre natural area river marsh."</ref><ref>Setha Low, Dana Taplin, Suzanne Scheld ''Rethinking Urban Parks: Public Space and Cultural Diversity'' 2009 p. 83 "...Liberty State Park, includes grass-covered fields, a public boat launch, walkways along the waterfront, spacious parking lots, and ... The other connecting corridor is the {{convert|1.3|mile|km}}-long Liberty Walk, a newly built promenade along the water's edge ..."</ref> this part of the project won a landscape award in 1995.<ref>Landscape Architecture Magazine 1995 "Wallace Roberts & Todd (WRT) of Philadelphia and New Jersey's Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) were the co-winners of a Top Honor Award for the overall plan and an Honor Award for Liberty State Park and Liberty Walk "</ref>

===Liberty Science Center===
[[Liberty Science Center]], which lies in the western portion of the park, is an interactive science museum and learning center. The center opened in 1993 as New Jersey's first major state [[science museum]]. It has science exhibits, the world's 5th largest [[IMAX Dome]] theater, the largest [[planetarium]] in the Western Hemisphere, numerous educational resources, and the original [[Hoberman sphere]], a silver, computer-driven engineering artwork designed by [[Chuck Hoberman]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nj.gov/dep/parksandforests/parks/liberty2.html |title=Liberty State Park |website=NJ Department of Parks and Forests |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517032810/http://www.nj.gov/dep/parksandforests/parks/liberty2.html |archive-date=May 17, 2011 |at=Liberty Science Center}}</ref> The museum also houses [[naked mole-rat]]s.

===Monuments and memorials===
[[Image:Liberation Statue 1.jpg|thumb|Liberation Memorial]]  [[File:Empty Sky P6150244.JPG|thumb|upright=1|''[[Empty Sky (memorial)|Empty Sky]]'', a memorial with a remnant from the [[World Trade Center (1973–2001)|World Trade Center]] in the foreground]]
''[[Liberation (Holocaust memorial)|Liberation]]'' is a 1985 bronze sculpture designed by [[Nathan Rapoport]] as a memorial to the [[Holocaust]], showing a U.S. soldier carrying out a survivor from a [[Nazism|Nazi]] death camp.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ettc.net/njarts/details.cfm?ID=424 |title=Art and Architecture of New Jersey |website=ETTC.net |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719035536/http://www.ettc.net/njarts/details.cfm?ID=424 |archive-date=July 19, 2011 |access-date=May 10, 2011}}</ref>

''[[La Vela di Colombo]]'' is a two-story sail-shaped bronze monument designed by Gino Gianetti that commemorates the 500th anniversary of the westward journey of [[Christopher Columbus]] to America in 1492. The "Sail of Columbus" sits atop a stone base in the shape of a ship and features scenes of Columbus and his travels. The gift from [[Government of Italy]] and the [[Genoa|City of Genoa]] was dedicated in 1998.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://njcu.libguides.com/jerseycitypastandpresent/libertystatepark|title=Liberty State Park|publisher=New Jersey City University|access-date=June 27, 2019|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190602040100/https://njcu.libguides.com/jerseycitypastandpresent/libertystatepark|archive-date=June 2, 2019}}</ref>

''[[Empty Sky (9-11 memorial)|Empty Sky]]'' is the official state memorial to the [[September 11 attacks]] of the [[World Trade Center (1973–2001)|World Trade Center]]. Situated on a berm the parallel walls engraved with the names of victims are oriented to face the former [[World Trade Center site]]. Designed by Jessica Jamroz and [[Frederic Schwartz]], it was dedicated on September 10, 2011, commemorating the tenth anniversary of the attacks.<ref name="nj">{{cite web |title=Liberty State Park |url=https://www.nj.gov/dep/parksandforests/parks/libertystatepark.html |access-date=June 23, 2025 |website=Official Site of the State of New Jersey}}</ref>

A temporary monument designed by [[Zaqistan|Zaq Landsberg]] called ''Reclining Liberty'' was displayed adjacent to ''[[Empty Sky (memorial)|Empty Sky]]'' May 2022 until April 2023. The monument, which shows the [[Statue of Liberty]] lying on her side, was previously on display in [[Harlem]]'s [[Marcus Garvey Park]] where it received attention from ''[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]]'' and ''[[Gothamist]]''. It was inspired by reclining Buddha statues in Asia as its intended meaning is to reconsider the meaning of the United States which, like the Statue of Liberty, is as Landsberg describes "an entity forever upright and tall."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hobokengirl.com/reclining-liberty-sculpture-jersey-city-liberty-state-park/|title=Reclining Liberty Comes to Liberty State Park in Jersey City|website=hobokengirl.com|date=June 28, 2022|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref>

==Liberty State Park Conservation, Recreation, and Community Inclusion Act==
[[File:Common tern in flight with Manhattan in the background.jpg|thumb|upright=1|A [[common tern]] seen from the park with [[Manhattan]] in the background]]
The [[Governorship of Chris Christie|administration of Governor Chris Christie]] proposed various commercial activities for the park.<ref>{{Cite web|title=1The Future of Liberty State Park:Creating a World Class Destination|url=http://media.nj.com/hudsoncountynow_impact/other/DEP%20LSP%20report.pdf|access-date=September 30, 2020|website=NJ.com}}</ref> In 2017, it suggested leasing large parts of the waterfront for private marinas.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2017/12/new_details_about_liberty_state_park_marina_emerge.html|title=Details emerge about new Liberty State Park marina| publisher= The Jersey Journal|last=McDonald|first=Terrence T.|date=December 7, 2017|website=NJ.com|access-date=December 8, 2017}}</ref>

Caven Point is a 22-acre man-made piece of land and sits adjacent to the [[Paul Fireman#Golf course development|Liberty National Golf Course]]. It is the only sandy beach along the shoreline and home to various migratory birds.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://hudsonreporter.com/2022/10/08/rallygoers-call-for-protection-of-caven-point-at-liberty-state-park/ | title=Rallygoers call for protection of Caven Point at Liberty State Park | date=October 9, 2022 |last=Koosau |first=Mark |website=Hudson Reporter |url-status=dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20221009055349/https://hudsonreporter.com/2022/10/08/rallygoers-call-for-protection-of-caven-point-at-liberty-state-park/|archive-date=October 9, 2022}}</ref> Proposals to protect the land have been made in the [[New Jersey Legislature]] such as the Liberty State Park Protection Act<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.njleg.state.nj.us/2020/Bills/A2500/2189_I1.HTM|title = A2189}}</ref> to specifically protect the park from all development without a severe vetting process and public scrutiny.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.njleg.state.nj.us/2018/Bills/S3500/3357_I1.HTM|title=Senate 3357|website=www.njleg.state.nj.us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.njleg.state.nj.us/2018/Bills/A5000/4903_I1.HTM|title=Assembly 4903|website=www.njleg.state.nj.us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nj.com/opinion/2021/12/ex-gov-whitman-protect-liberty-state-park-so-we-all-can-enjoy-this-gem-opinion.html|title = Ex-Gov. Whitman: Protect Liberty State Park so we all can enjoy this gem | Opinion| newspaper=Nj |date = December 7, 2021 |last=Whitman |first=Christine Todd |authorlink=Christine Todd Whitman}}</ref>
That proposal has been rejected by both the senate and the assembly for its exclusion of the surrounding community.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2022/06/bill-advances-that-would-allow-commercial-development-at-liberty-state-park.html | title=Bill advances that could allow privatization of Liberty State Park | date=June 16, 2022 | last=Maher | first=Jake | website=NJ.com}}</ref> The Liberty State Park Conservation, Recreation, and Community Inclusion Act was passed in July 2022 with and as a result of the local community feeling it had been left out of the conversation for decades would now be a part of the decision making within this park.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://hudsonreporter.com/2022/06/23/controversial-liberty-state-park-bill-advances-through-state-committees/ | title=Controversial Liberty State Park bill advances through state committees | date=June 24, 2022 | last=Koosau | first=Mark | website=Hudson Reporter}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://hudsonreporter.com/2022/06/30/state-legislature-passes-bill-to-redevelop-liberty-state-park/ | title=Gov. Phil Murphy signs bill to redevelop Liberty State Park | date=June 30, 2022 | last=Koosau | first=Mark | website=Hudson Reporter}}</ref> The Liberty State Park Conservation, Recreation, and Community Inclusion Act establishes a 17-member Liberty State Park Design Task Force within the [[New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection]] (NJDEP) to assist with developing short-term plans to improve public use at the park. In 2023, the Commissioner of the NJDEP, Shawn LaTourette, assured the public that while active recreation facilities will be added to specific areas of the park, they will not be for-profit private facilities.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hudsoncountyview.com/liberty-state-park-revitalization-will-include-arts-athletics-but-no-privatization/|title=Liberty State Park revitalization will include arts & athletics, but no privatization|website=hudsoncountyview.com|date=May 25, 2023|access-date=July 11, 2025}}</ref>

==Transportation==
[[image:Liberty State Park HBLR Station.jpg|thumb|left|Liberty State Park HBLR Station]]
[[NJ Transit]]'s [[Hudson-Bergen Light Rail]] runs just to the west of the park. The park is served by the [[Hudson–Bergen Light Rail#Routes|West Side Avenue–Tonnelle Avenue]] and [[Hudson–Bergen Light Rail#Routes|8th Street–Hoboken Terminal]] trains at the [[Liberty State Park (HBLR station)|Liberty State Park station]] at the park's western entrance.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kaulessar |first=Ricardo |date=September 6, 2009 |title=Trolley through Liberty State Park? |newspaper=[[The Hudson Reporter]]|location=[[Bayonne]]|language=en-US|url-status=live|url=https://archive.hudsonreporter.com/2009/09/06/trolley-through-liberty-state-park/|accessdate=March 12, 2022|archivedate=March 12, 2022|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220312151558/https://archive.hudsonreporter.com/2009/09/06/trolley-through-liberty-state-park/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Most|first=Doug|title=At Last, A Trolley Runs Through It|work=[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]]|location=Bergen County |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P1-26031162.html|language=en-US|url-status=usurped|date=April 16, 2000|access-date=March 12, 2022|archive-date=October 19, 2012|via=[[HighBeam Research]]|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019205001/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P1-26031162.html}}</ref> The park is also served by the [[List of New Jersey Transit bus routes (1-99)|16]] [[New Jersey Transit Bus Operations|NJ Transit Bus]] route at the station.

The park is served by the [[Liberty Landing Ferry]] with service to [[Liberty Harbor]] in Downtown Jersey City at Warren Street and [[Battery Park City Ferry Terminal|Battery Park City]] in [[Lower Manhattan]]. Various harbor cruises also depart from the landing.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kilgannon |first=Corey |last2=Cohen |first2=Miles G. |date=August 16, 2026 |title=It's a Crowded Place With Some of the City's Trickiest Traffic |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/16/nyregion/new-york-harbor-safety.html |access-date=August 16, 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

Since 2024, a free shuttle bus service, provided by EZ Ride, operates on weekends and holidays from April to November connecting various points of interest within the park to Hudson-Bergen Light Rail and NJ Transit Bus service at Liberty State Park station and ferry service at Liberty Landing. Prior to this service, a pay-to-ride NJ Transit shuttle service operated at the park from 2000 until 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2024/07/free-shuttle-service-begins-inside-liberty-state-park.html|title=Free shuttle service inside Liberty State Park begins today|publisher=The Jersey Journal|date=July 19, 2024|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ezride.org/routes/257-liberty-state-park-shuttle/|title=257: Liberty State Park Shuttle|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref> In July 2012, [[North Jersey Transportation Planning Authority|NJTPA]] allotted $175,000 to study transportation alternatives to and within the park.<ref>{{cite news|first=Alyana|last=Cronk|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2012/07/jersey_city_receives_grant_to.html|title=Jersey City receives $175,000 state grant to study public-transportation options in Liberty State Park|date=July 20, 2021|newspaper=The Jersey Journal|access-date=September 13, 2021}}</ref> 

In May 2013, a new pedestrian bridge, the "Ethel Pesin Liberty Footbridge", named after the late wife of the state park's founder Morris Pesin, was placed over Mill Creek at the Morris Canal Basin to replace an older one that had been destroyed by [[Superstorm Sandy]] in October 2012. The new bridge reconnected the northwestern edge of Libery State Park with Downtown Jersey City and was situated so as not interfere with any new road construction.<ref>{{cite news|last = McDonald|first=Terrence T.|title=Seven months after Sandy, a new $800K bridge in Jersey City|newspaper = The Jersey Journal|date = May 23, 2013|url = http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2013/05/seven_months_after_sandy_a_new.html |access-date=September 13, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Mill Creek Footbridge|url=http://www.bridgesnyc.com/2013/05/mill-creek-footbridge/|website=bridgesnyc.com|date=May 27, 2013|access-date=January 22, 2015}}</ref>

[[Image:Liberty State Park Bridge over the Morris Canal Basin, Jersey City NJ 20250511-jag9889.jpg|thumb|upright=1|Liberty State Park Bridge over the Morris Canal Basin (opened 2021)]]

The park is accessible by car via several local roads and the [[New Jersey Turnpike]] ([[Interstate 78 in New Jersey|I-78]]) at Exits 14B and 14C. In March 2013, Jersey City received a $500,000 grant to study the extension of Jersey Avenue directly into the park, to simplify access from the [[Downtown Jersey City|Downtown]] neighborhoods, facilitate through traffic to and from [[Communipaw]], and provide alternatives for Turnpike users to access Downtown Jersey City.<ref>{{cite news|first=Terrence T. | last=McDonald|url=http://www.nj.com/jjournal-news/index.ssf/2013/03/jersey_city_gets_500000_federa.html|title=Jersey City gets $500K federal grant to study extension of road into Liberty State Park|date=March 19, 2013|newspaper=The Jersey Journal|access-date=September 13, 2021}}</ref><ref name="nj.com">{{cite news|last1=McDonald|first1=Terrence T.|title=$10M bridge connecting Downtown Jersey City to Liberty State Park closer to reality|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2014/08/bridge_connecting_downtown_jersey_city_into_liberty_state_park_closer_to_reality.html|access-date=January 22, 2015|newspaper=The Jersey Journal|date=August 22, 2014}}</ref>

In 2014 NJDOT announced that it would build a $10 million bridge over the [[Morris Canal|Morris Canal Basin]], reducing the commute between the park and [[Downtown Jersey City]] by more than half a mile.<ref name="nj.com"/> Construction of the connection between Jersey Ave and Phillip Street began in August 2019; the two-lane road with adjoining bike lanes and sidewalks was opened to traffic in August 2021.<ref>{{cite news | last = Zeitlinger|first = Ron|title = After decades of talk, road project connecting Downtown to Liberty State Park, Bergen-Laf is underway |newspaper = The Jersey Journal|date = August 7, 2019 | url = https://www.nj.com/hudson/2019/08/after-decades-of-talk-road-project-connecting-downtown-to-liberty-state-park-bergen-laf-is-underway.html | access-date = September 13, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Adler | first=Egan | title = Opening up a whole new avenue of access to Downtown Jersey City and Liberty State Park | newspaper = The Jersey Journal | date = July 30, 2021|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2021/07/opening-up-a-whole-new-avenue-of-access-to-downtown-jersey-city-and-liberty-state-park.html| access-date=September 13, 2021}}</ref> Since the opening, residents have complained about safety concerns and an increase in traffic congestion due to [[Holland Tunnel]]-bound traffic connecting to I-78 through the park. Prior to the bridge, the Mayor [[Steven Fulop]] announced the city administration is experimenting with traffic light timing and collaborating with navigation service [[Waze]] to reduce congestion.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=StevenFulop |author=Steven Fulop |number=1445338971253391364 |date=October 5, 2021 |access-date=October 9, 2021 |title=We are very much on top of it/aware. Last weekend we experimented with traffic light timing changes. When comparing data from Sunday, 9/26 (normal signal timing) + Sunday, 10/3 (modified timing), there were 845 fewer vehicles, which equals a 23% decrease.}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |user=StevenFulop |author=Steven Fulop |number=1445338974516654080 |date=October 5, 2021 |access-date=October 9, 2021 |title=Also we are working with Google maps + Waze – just wanted to let you know that we are optimistic that we will be able to get this right for everyone |link=no}}</ref>

==In popular culture==
[[Image:YuvrajrDowntownJerseyCityLSP5.JPG|thumb|upright=1|[[Liberty Harbor]]]]
On [[Labor Day (United States)|Labor Day]] in 1980, Republican Nominee for President [[Ronald Reagan]] kicked off his national campaign on Liberty Island, with the Statue of Liberty behind him and said: 'I want more than anything I've ever wanted, to have an administration that will, through its actions, at home and in the international arena, let millions of people know that Miss Liberty still "Lifts her lamp beside the golden door."'<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.reagan.utexas.edu/archives/reference/9.1.80.html|title=9/1/1980 Speech|website=www.reagan.UTexas.edu|access-date=December 8, 2017|archive-date=March 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150308151237/http://www.reagan.utexas.edu/archives/reference/9.1.80.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2002, [[Budweiser]] filmed two commercials to dedicate the [[September 11 attacks]] in the park (one in 2002, and another one in 2011). Both were only aired once.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aol.com/article/finance/2017/09/11/the-story-behind-the-911-budweiser-commercial-that-only-aired-once/23204869/|title=The true story behind the 9/11 Budweiser commercial that only aired once|author=A. O. L. Staff|website=AOL.com|language=en|access-date=January 27, 2019|archive-date=October 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022131335/https://www.aol.com/article/finance/2017/09/11/the-story-behind-the-911-budweiser-commercial-that-only-aired-once/23204869/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Since 2015, the park has hosted festivities as part of New York City's annual [[Fleet Week#New York City|Fleet Week]] celebration.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2019/05/liberty-state-park-has-races-music-and-demos-galore-on-sunday-for-fleet-week.html|title=Liberty State Park has races, music and demos galore on Sunday for Fleet Week|publisher=The Jersey Journal|date=May 23, 2019|access-date=July 1, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://patch.com/new-jersey/jersey-city/fleet-weeks-coming-liberty-state-park-jersey-city-weekend|title=Fleet Week's Coming To The Jersey City Side This Weekend: Demonstrations And More|website=patch.com|date=May 22, 2025|access-date=July 1, 2025}}</ref>

The concert was later broadcast on [[HBO]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/news/2023/11/remembering-hall-oates-epic-nj-concert-as-the-feuding-duo-heads-to-court.html|title=Remembering Hall & Oates' epic N.J. concert as the feuding duo heads to court|website=nj.com|date=November 30, 2023|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref>

* In 2012, [[Aretha Franklin]] performed at the park for the Fourth Annual Celebrating Life and Liberty event, hosted by the [[John Theurer Cancer Center]] at [[Hackensack University Medical Center]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/jjournal-news/2012/10/aretha_franklin_performs_for_c.html|title=Aretha Franklin performs for cancer survivors at Liberty State Park|publisher=The Jersey Journal|date=October 1, 2012|access-date=July 10, 2025}}</ref>
* In 2013, [[Cher]], [[Tim McGraw]], [[Miguel (singer)|Miguel]], [[Mariah Carey]] and [[Selena Gomez]] performed at the park for the [[Macy's 4th of July Fireworks|Macy's 4th of July Fireworks Spectacular]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=July 4, 2013|first=Amy|last=Sciarretto|title=Selena Gomez Performs 'Come & Get It' + 'Slow Down' at Macy's 4th of July Fireworks Spectacular|url=https://popcrush.com/selena-gomez-come-get-it-slow-down-macys-4th-of-july-fireworks-spectacular/|access-date=September 6, 2020|website=PopCrush|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=September 28, 2013|title=Mariah Carey Live @ Macy's 4th of July concert on NBC|website=[[YouTube]]|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eyMgEubHWKk |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/eyMgEubHWKk |archive-date=December 21, 2021 |url-status=live}}{{cbignore}}</ref>
* Jersey City's Freedom and Fireworks Festival debuted in the park in 2013 [[Independence Day (United States)|Independence Day]] and included performances from [[Fireworks by Grucci]] and the Jersey City-based [[Kool & the Gang]]. Since 2017, the festival has been held in the city's [[Exchange Place, Jersey City|Exchange Place]] neighborhood.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Lustig|first=Jay|date=July 3, 2017|title=Government shutdown forces Freedom Fireworks Festival, featuring Kool and the Gang, to move|url=https://www.njarts.net/pop-rock/government-shutdown-forces-freedom-fireworks-festival-featuring-kool-gang-move/|access-date=September 6, 2020|website=NJArts.net|language=en-US}}</ref>

* Since 2023, the park hosts the annual [[Juneteenth]] All About Us Festival having featured performances from [[Musiq Soulchild]], [[Crystal Waters]], [[Robin S.]], [[Mario (American singer)|Mario]] and [[Jadakiss]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tapinto.net/towns/jersey-city/sections/arts-and-entertainment/articles/jersey-city-s-all-about-us-festival-brought-community-together-for-juneteenth-in-liberty-state-park|title=Jersey City's All About Us Festival Brought Community Together for Juneteenth in Liberty State Park|website=tapinto.com/jersey-city|date=June 30, 2024|access-date=June 20, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://hudsoncountyview.com/jadakiss-mario-headline-juneteenth-all-about-us-festival-at-liberty-state-park/|title=Jadakiss & Mario headline Juneteenth 'All About Us Festival' at Liberty State Park|website=hudsoncountyview.com|date=June 18, 2025|access-date=June 20, 2025}}</ref>

Take the cannoli", was filmed at the site before the construction of Liberty State Park.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scoutingny.com/the-godfather-the-new-york-city-filming-locations-then-and-now/2/|title=The New York Filming Locations of The Godfather, Then and Now – Scouting NY – Page 2|website=www.ScoutingNY.com|date=January 26, 2014|access-date=December 8, 2017}}</ref>

Tune in for complete coverage live from Liberty State Park!"|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CHFuliKhLO3/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/CHFuliKhLO3 |archive-date=December 24, 2021 |url-access=limited| access-date=July 11, 2025| website=Instagram| language=en}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

===Sports===
* Since 2007, the [[Veuve Clicquot]] Polo Classic is held every Spring at Liberty State Park.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2018/06/veuve_clicquot_polo_classic_returns_to_liberty_sta.html|title=Veuve Clicquot Polo Classic returns to Liberty State Park with star-studded guest list (PHOTOS)|publisher=The Jersey Journal|last=McDonald|first=Corey W. |date=June 2, 2018|access-date=June 4, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://theknockturnal.com/veuve-clicquot-polo-classic-ignites-summer-season-in-style/|title=Veuve Clicquot Polo Classic Ignites Summer Season in Style-The beloved annual event returned to Liberty State Park|website=theknockturnal.com|date=June 5, 2023|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref>
* In May 2010, plans were put forth outlining the use of the park as the new home of the [[United States Grand Prix|United States]] [[Formula One]] [[Grand Prix motor racing|Grand Prix]] for the [[2012 Formula One season|2012 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=New York F1 track plans revealed – Jersey City bids for 2012 night race|url=http://www.f1fanatic.co.uk/2010/05/04/new-york-f1-track-plans-revealed-jersey-city-bids-for-new-night-race-in-2012/|first=Keith|last=Collantine|work=F1 Fanatic|publisher=Keith Collantine|date=May 4, 2010|access-date=May 4, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100709062753/http://www.f1fanatic.co.uk/2010/05/04/new-york-f1-track-plans-revealed-jersey-city-bids-for-new-night-race-in-2012/|archive-date=July 9, 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> These plans met outrage from the community, particularly the Friends of Liberty State Park, and were ultimately rejected by the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.folsp.org/preservation/grand_prix.htm|title=folsp.org|website=FOLSP.org|access-date=December 8, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130605174724/http://www.folsp.org/preservation/grand_prix.htm|archive-date=June 5, 2013}}</ref>
* On June 19 and 20, 2010, the park hosted the fifth round of the [[2010 Red Bull Air Race World Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2010/06/countdown_to_jersey_city_red_b.html|title=About the Red Bull Air Race in Jersey City|newspaper=The Jersey Journal|last=Hayes|first=Melissa|date=June 4, 2010|access-date=June 18, 2018}}</ref>
* Since 2019, the park's Liberty Landing Marina has been the home base for teams competing in the New York leg of the annual [[Sail GP]] international [[Sailing (sport)|sailing]] competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sail-world.com/news/218732/US-SailGP-Team-showcases-Lady-Liberty|title=U.S. SailGP Team showcases "Lady Liberty" on the Hudson ahead of first-ever New York City race|website=sail-world.com|date=June 18, 2019|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://visitnyc.com/sports/sailgp-2025-thrilling-races-in-new-york-harbor-8923/|title=SailGP 2025: Thrilling Races in New York Harbor|website=visitnyc.com|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref>
* In 2026, the park was planned to host the [[FIFA Fan Festival]] for the [[New York metropolitan area|New York/New Jersey]] area as part of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], but this was cancelled.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/feb/11/2026-world-cup-fan-fest-new-jersey|title=New Jersey to host 2026 World Cup fan fest at Liberty State Park|agency=Associated Press|date=February 11, 2025|via=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.frontrowsoccer.com/2025/06/11/give-them-liberty-ny-nj-fifa-fan-festival-to-be-at-liberty-state-park/|title=GIVE THEM LIBERTY: NY/NJ FIFA Fan Festival to be at Liberty State Park|website=frontrowsoccer.com|date=June 11, 2025|access-date=June 16, 2025}}</ref>
